gate_2_plant_rate.claim: a grammar bug is caught on every run of the round-trip property
gate_2_plant_rate.case: tests/unit/test_unit_grammar.py's round-trip property run under each of three planted parser bugs: '/' distributing over only the first factor of a parenthesised group; '^' dropped on a parenthesised group; a quotient's right-hand side added instead of subtracted

prediction.unit: caught out of 30 fresh processes, each with its own Hypothesis seed
prediction.why: unit_symbol writes a parenthesis only where the dimension has none of its own symbols, which the drawn dimensions reach in most draws; but 'equivalent spellings parse equal' is a table of cases that holds the plants on every run, so the property's rate is the lower number and the test's the upper

gate_2_plant_rate.metric: caught / runs from .github/probe/detection_rate.py, with the clean arm at 0/30

control.plant: as above, switched on by MIME_PLANT_UNIT_GRAMMAR

gate_2_plant_rate.if_wrong: a rate below 30/30 is a plant the draws do not reach: strengthen the table of cases or the strategy, never filter the draws
gate_2_plant_rate.cannot_discriminate_if: the property draws only dimensions whose symbols are named (no parenthesis written)

gate_3_import_time.claim: labels checked at definition add no measurable time to `import mime`
gate_3_import_time.case: python -X importtime-free wall clock of `python -c 'import mime'`, median of 15 runs, base and head alternating, on this machine, nothing else of mine running

prediction.why: only the vocabulary's Interface entries (about 40) parse at import: every Units(...) sits in an annotation the modules postpone (from __future__ import annotations), so it is built when the typed state is first read, not at import; 40 parses of strings under 30 characters cost well under 5 ms, against an import of seconds. The machine is shared with other sessions, so the run-to-run spread, not the parse, sets the band.

gate_3_import_time.metric: median wall time of 15 alternating runs, with their spread

control.plant: a 50 ms sleep added to the vocabulary's define()
control.expected_rate: the measured difference is above 0.04 s

gate_3_import_time.if_wrong: a difference above 0.05 s would mean the parse is slower than derived, or the import path moved
gate_3_import_time.cannot_discriminate_if: the spread of the 15 runs is over 0.05 s: the measurement then bounds the difference from above only, and says so
